round: 5 — the structural forward merge of #2179, review round 4's two findings (one a path traversal), and the architect's three items

proof.criterion: The merged store rule: a session store that keeps sessions in a database is required, and `pvc` is refused — not `postgres` demanded, since #2179's `cloudsql-iam` keeps sessions off the disk exactly as `postgres` does.
proof.surface: The real CLI surface, `legion start --check-config`, over five configurations built from the shipped `deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example`.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go build -o /legion/scratch/tmp/legion-head ./cmd/legion; then legion start --check-config --config {postgres,cloudsql,pvc,omitted,unknown}.yaml
proof.observed: postgres → `Config OK: project=WIDGETS`; cloudsql-iam → `Config OK`; pvc → `legion start: runtime.kubernetes.session_store must name a store that keeps sessions in a database, and is required (INFRA-80): an issue pod's disk is the pod's own ephemeral volume, deleted with the pod, so a session kept as a file on it ('pvc', also what an omitted session_store means) dies with it, the next launch's resume fails on the missing file (internal/launcher's sessionWritten), and three such failures retire the claim`; an omitted session_store → the same refusal; `mysql` → main's own unchanged error, `must be 'pvc', 'postgres' or 'cloudsql-iam'`.
proof.negativeControl: A `legion` built from `main@origin` (0306bcbe16df), run against the same two files, answers `Config OK: project=WIDGETS` for both `pvc` and the omitted store. The refusal is this change's, measured rather than asserted.

proof.criterion: The e2e session exporter cannot write a host file outside the evidence directory, whatever key the session database holds — review round 4's security finding.
proof.surface: The real `session_copy` taken from `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh` by name, driven into a destination nested inside a fresh temporary root with a sentinel file beside it, with the filesystem walked afterwards.
proof.observed: 22 pass. Crafted keys: `../`, absolute after the prefix, an embedded newline, bytes past ASCII, and the `.`/`..`/empty/collision refusals, plus a symlink planted in the destination. Nothing appeared outside the destination in any case; the sentinel's bytes are unchanged; each refusal names the key and not the session's bytes.
proof.negativeControl: Against the unfixed function in a scratch copy of the script, `12 fail, 10 pass`, the four traversal cases among the failures. That control was run twice: the first run passed 22/22 because a failed `cp` had left the fixed script in place, so it had proved nothing. The second was run with the unfixed function confirmed in place by grep first.

proof.criterion: The test fixture builds the architecture this change makes, and the migration tests still exercise the superseded one.
proof.surface: The sandbox package's own suite, and a grep over the daemon module.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox; grep -rn 'withoutVolume' packages/daemon/
proof.observed: The suite passes and the grep is empty. `sandboxObject` builds an issue Sandbox with no claim template; `withSupersededDisk` is the named opt-in at three call sites; `cleanup_test` models each issue's disk through its pod, as the runtime does.

The pull request body: `CI`, `Threads`, `E2E (implementer)`, `Chain`, `Size`, the census's store sentence, and a compressed sweep section. Plus a comment carrying the Stage 4a runner's revised check list.
trickyParts: The merge's one decision was not a conflict-resolution detail: this branch's refusal was spelled `session_store must be 'postgres'`, which after #2179 would refuse `cloudsql-iam` — a store whose sessions survive the pod exactly as `postgres`'s do. The rule is 'not pvc', and the message states the mechanism and names no permitted spelling, so a fourth store kind needs no edit here.

A key holding a newline could not be fixed by checking keys: psql prints one row a line, so such a key arrived as two keys before any check could see it. The listing returns `encode(convert_to(path,'UTF8'),'hex')` and the reader decodes byte for byte under `LC_ALL=C`.

The fixture inversion's one failure mode is a migration test that silently stops exercising the superseded shape. It is checked rather than asserted: the replacement test requires a delete-then-create that a Sandbox owning no claim template never produces.
deviations: The first negative control for the traversal fix was invalid and passed 22/22: a failed `cp` in its setup had left the fixed script in place. It is recorded here and in the thread reply because an invalid control that passes is indistinguishable from a valid one, and because it is the near miss that makes the real control meaningful.

I published a pull request body built on a copy fetched two minutes earlier, and the live body had shrunk by 279 characters in between, so an edit by another role may have been overwritten. GitHub exposes no body history; I have told the reviewer exactly what I published and asked it to name anything of its own that is missing.
Every proof of the earlier rounds was re-run rather than carried: they were taken against a `legion` built from heads that no longer exist.
openQuestions: Stage 4b is repaired and has run at no head, here or anywhere. `shellcheck` is not installed in this pod (`command -v shellcheck` returns nothing), so the scripts have `bash -n` and `bunx biome check scripts/e2e/lib` only.

Stage 4a's seven inverted checks are still unrun; the one live attempt died at `root-ready` before reaching them. The revised check list for the runner is a comment on the pull request, marking each of the 65 rows changed or unchanged, measured by command rather than by reading: 13 changed, one renamed, one new.
The reviewer's round-4 review body had not been submitted when this round completed; only its two inline threads were visible, and both are answered and resolved.
discoveredComplexity: A repair is new code and gets the scrutiny new code gets — which is exactly the scrutiny a repair tends not to get, because everyone reads it as a fix to something already reviewed. The session exporter was written last round to repair a broken proof and shipped a path traversal, found by review rather than by the person who wrote it. This belongs in the issue's retro note as its own entry.

An invalid negative control that passes is indistinguishable from a valid one, and it is the only check whose failure mode is silence in both directions. Both halves of the near miss belong in the note: the control that passed because the setup had failed, and the real one that gave 12 fail, 10 pass.

Two changes rewriting the same mechanism in parallel resolve cleanly and can still mean something neither author intended. Here they met over how a store is named and projected and nowhere over who owns the disk, which was read in the other change's source rather than inferred from its title — but the one place they did meet carried a rule that would have refused a store the deployment intends to use.
